title: DNS CLI (dig, host, nslookup)
intro: Work from the module directory. Fixtures: **`dig_cname_a.txt`**, **`dig_mx.txt`**, **`host_out.txt`**, **`nslookup_out.txt`**, **`dig_multi_rr.txt`**.

questions.prompt: From **`dig_cname_a.txt`**, print the **`;; ANSWER SECTION:`** line and every line until (not including) the **next** line starting **`;;`**.
questions.expectedOutput:
;; ANSWER SECTION:
www.lab.example. 300 IN CNAME edge.lab.example.
edge.lab.example. 60 IN A 198.51.100.7
questions.solutionMarkdown: Slice from **`;; ANSWER SECTION:`** through the last RR before **`;; Query`**.

questions.prompt: Same span as **1**, but print **only** the **resource-record** lines (omit the **`;; ANSWER SECTION:`** header).
questions.expectedOutput:
www.lab.example. 300 IN CNAME edge.lab.example.
edge.lab.example. 60 IN A 198.51.100.7
questions.solutionMarkdown: Same block as **q1** without the section header line.

questions.prompt: From **`dig_cname_a.txt`**, print **only** the **TTL** (second field) of each ANSWER RR line, **one per line**, file order.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Second column on RR lines in the ANSWER section.

questions.prompt: From **`dig_cname_a.txt`**, print the **record type** (field after **`IN`**) for each ANSWER RR line, one per line, file order.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Fourth field on standard **`dig`** RR lines.

questions.prompt: From **`dig_cname_a.txt`**, for each ANSWER line whose type is **`CNAME`**, print **`owner<TAB>target`** (last field is target). Use a **literal tab** between owner and target.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Owner is column 1; CNAME rdata is the final field.

questions.prompt: From **`dig_cname_a.txt`**, print the **IPv4** (last field) of every ANSWER line whose type is **`A`**, one per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Filter **`A`** rows; print the address field.

questions.prompt: From **`dig_mx.txt`**, for each ANSWER **`MX`** line, print **preference** and **mail exchanger hostname** as **two fields separated by a single space**, file order.
From **`host_out.txt`**, print the **IPv4** at the end of every line containing **`has address `** (trailing space; not **`has IPv6 address`**), one per line, file order.
From **`nslookup_out.txt`**, print the **IPv4** on the line that begins with **`Address:`** (second whitespace-delimited field).
questions.solutionMarkdown: Pick the **`Address:`** line with an IPv4 literal.

questions.prompt: From **`dig_multi_rr.txt`**, collect the TTL (second field) of each ANSWER RR line; print **unique** values **sorted numerically ascending**, one per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Unique TTLs from the ANSWER RRs, **`sort -n`**.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes

- Read **`dig`** output: header, **`;; QUESTION SECTION:`**, **`;; ANSWER SECTION:`**, TTL, class, type, and RDATA.
- Follow a **CNAME** chain in answer data and relate it to the final **A** (or **AAAA**) record.
- Use **`host`** and legacy **`nslookup`** output for quick lookups when **`dig`** is not the habit.
- Understand **TTL** as cache hint (stale vs fresh answers is resolver policy, not re-queried every second).

## Scope

**In scope:** CLI output shapes, parsing fixtures, common record types (**A**, **AAAA**, **CNAME**, **MX**, **NS**, **TXT** at a glance). **Out of scope:** DNSSEC chain validation, zone authoring, authoritative vs recursive server administration.

## Concept outline

1. **Recursive vs authoritative** — who answers your laptop query; why you see “Non-authoritative answer” from resolvers.
2. **`dig` flags** — **`+short`**, **`+noall +answer`**, **`+trace`** (concept: iterative resolution path); server selection **`@resolver`**.
3. **Record lines** — owner name, TTL, class (**IN**), type, RDATA (type-dependent columns).
4. **CNAME** — alias owner points to another name; final answers often end in **A**/**AAAA**.
5. **`host`** — terse, human-oriented; **`nslookup`** — interactive legacy; both still appear in docs and old scripts.

## Tooling and alternatives

| Task | Primary | Notes |
|------|---------|--------|
| Scripted / precise output | **`dig`** | Widely installed; stable **`;;` sections**. |
| Quick name → address | **`host`** | Fewer columns; easy **`grep`**. |
| Legacy / Windows habits | **`nslookup`** | Mixed formatting; fine for ad hoc use. |
| macOS resolver DB | **`dscacheutil -q host -a name …`** | Not a substitute for learning **`dig`** output. |
